|website=[[Google Doodle]] |url=https://doodles.google/doodle/sally-rides-64th-birthday/ |access-date=July 28, 2022 |archive-date=December 18, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231218045406/https://doodles.google/doodle/sally-rides-64th-birthday/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It was reused on [[International Women's Day]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=International Women's Day 2017 |url=https://doodles.google/doodle/international-womens-day-2017/ |website=[[Google Doodle]] |access-date=March 8, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506073920/https://www.google.com/doodles/international-womens-day-2017 |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |date=March 8, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> Stanford University's Serra House, located in Lucie Stern Hall, was renamed the Sally Ride House in 2019.<ref name="mercurynews1">{{cite news |last1=Green |first1=Jason |title=Stanford renames buildings for Sally Ride, Carolyn Attneave |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2019/03/01/stanford-renames-buildings-for-sally-ride-carolyn-attneave/ |access-date=March 2, 2019 |newspaper=[[The Mercury News]] |publisher=[[Digital First Media]] |date=March 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506074531/https://www.mercurynews.com/2019/03/01/stanford-renames-buildings-for-sally-ride-carolyn-attneave/ |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |location=San Jose, California |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[U.S. Postal Service]] issued a first-class postage stamp honoring her in 2018,<ref name="spo20180523">{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Marcia |title=Today's Tidbits: May 23, 2018 |url=https://spacepolicyonline.com/news/todays-tidbits-may-23-2018/ |website=SpacePolicyOnline.com |access-date=May 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506074208/https://spacepolicyonline.com/news/todays-tidbits-may-23-2018/ |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |date=May 23, 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> and Ride appeared as one of the first two honorees of the [[American Women quarters]] series in March 2022, the first known LGBT person to appear on U.S. currency.<ref name="usmint">{{cite press release |title=United States Mint Announces First Two Honorees in American Women Quarters Program |url=https://www.usmint.gov/news/press-releases/united-states-mint-announces-first-two-honorees-in-american-women-quarters-program |publisher=[[United States Mint]] |access-date=April 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506080522/https://www.usmint.gov/news/press-releases/united-states-mint-announces-first-two-honorees-in-american-women-quarters-program |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |location=Washington, D.C. |date=April 12, 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite press release |title=Dr. Sally Ride Quarter Begins Shipping |publisher=[[United States Mint]] |url=https://www.usmint.gov/news/press-releases/united-states-mint-begins-shipping-american-women-quarters-program-coins-honoring-dr-sally-ride |access-date=July 23, 2022 |archive-date=July 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220722232614/https://www.usmint.gov/news/press-releases/united-states-mint-begins-shipping-american-women-quarters-program-coins-honoring-dr-sally-ride |url-status=live }}</ref>

On April 1, 2022, a satellite named after Ride ([[ÑuSat|ÑuSat 27]] or "Sally", COSPAR 2022-033R) was launched into space as part of the [[Satellogic]] Aleph-1 constellation.<ref name="Kramer 2020">{{cite web |last=Kramer |first=Herbert J. |title=Satellogic-Nusat |website=eoPortal |date=September 15, 2020 |url=https://www.eoportal.org/satellite-missions/satellogic#sensor-complement-imager |access-date=November 3, 2022 }}</ref>

The [[Cygnus spacecraft]] used for the [[Cygnus NG-18|NG-18]] mission was named the S.S. ''Sally Ride'' in her honor. It launched successfully on November 7, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NASA Commercial Resupply Mission NG-18 |url=https://www.northropgrumman.com/space/nasa-commercial-resupply-mission-ng-18 |access-date=November 7, 2022 |website=Northrop Grumman |language=en-US |archive-date=November 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221106130857/https://www.northropgrumman.com/space/nasa-commercial-resupply-mission-ng-18/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2022, a statue of Ride was unveiled outside the [[Cradle of Aviation Museum]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/dr-sally-ride-statue/ |title=Dr. Sally Ride honored with statue at Cradle of Aviation Museum in Garden City - CBS New York |date=June 17, 2022 |website=www.cbsnews.com |access-date=September 12, 2022 |archive-date=February 18, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250218082019/https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/dr-sally-ride-statue/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, another statue of Ride was unveiled, outside the [[Ronald Reagan Presidential Library]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/video/sally-ride-statue-unveiled-in-california/ |title=Sally Ride statue unveiled in California - CBS News |website=www.cbsnews.com }}</ref>

== In popular culture ==
*The 1989 [[Billy Joel]] song "[[We Didn't Start the Fire]]" mentions Ride.
* Ride appeared as herself in the 1999 ''[[Touched by an Angel]]'' episode "Godspeed".<ref name="Sherr2014" />{{rp|p=299}}
* Astronauts [[Chris Hadfield]] and [[Catherine Coleman]] performed a song called "Ride On".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jaworski |first1=Michelle |title=8 reasons Chris Hadfield is the coolest astronaut on the Web |url=https://www.dailydot.com/upstream/chris-hadfield-astronaut-iss-reddit-ama/ |website=[[The Daily Dot]] |access-date=May 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506082254/https://www.dailydot.com/upstream/chris-hadfield-astronaut-iss-reddit-ama/ |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |location=Austin, Texas |date=March 2, 2020 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mA9dROqvC0k |title='Ride On' by Astronauts Chris Hadfield and Catherine Coleman |date=January 5, 2013 |publisher=Rare Earth |via=YouTube |access-date=May 2, 2023 |archive-date=June 2, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602185230/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mA9dROqvC0k |url-status=live }}</ref> The song was later released as part of Hadfield's album ''Space Sessions: Songs from a Tin Can'' under the name "Ride That Lightning."<ref name="exclaim">{{cite web |last1=Hudson |first1=Alex |title=Chris Hadfield – "Ride That Lightning" (lyric video) |url=https://exclaim.ca/music/article/chris_hadfield-ride_that_lightning_lyric_video |website=[[Exclaim!]] |access-date=October 30, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506082555/https://exclaim.ca/music/article/chris_hadfield-ride_that_lightning_lyric_video |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |location=Toronto |date=September 11, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* In the 2013 TV movie ''[[The Challenger Disaster]]'' she was portrayed by [[Eve Best]].<ref>{{cite news |first=David |last=Wiegand |title='The Challenger Disaster' review: A true thriller |date=November 13, 2013 |website=sfgate.com |url=https://www.sfgate.com/tv/article/The-Challenger-Disaster-review-A-true-thriller-4981585.php |access-date=November 9, 2025 |archive-date=March 23, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230323021518/https://www.sfgate.com/tv/article/The-Challenger-Disaster-review-A-true-thriller-4981585.php |url-status=live }}</ref>
* A 2017 "Women of NASA" [[Lego]] set featured mini-figurines of Ride, [[Margaret Hamilton (software engineer)|Margaret Hamilton]], [[Mae Jemison]], and [[Nancy Roman]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mosher |first1=Dave |title=Lego's 'Women of NASA' toy set is finally on sale – and it's already Amazon's best-selling toy |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/lego-female-scientists-engineers-nasa-kit-2017-11 |website=[[Business Insider]] |access-date=May 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506083555/https://www.businessinsider.com/lego-female-scientists-engineers-nasa-kit-2017-11 |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |date=November 3, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* In 2019, [[Mattel]] released a [[Barbie]] doll in Ride's likeness as part of their "Inspiring Women" series.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://wjla.com/news/entertainment/barbie-launches-new-inspiring-women-dolls-honoring-rosa-parks-sally-ride |title=Barbie launches new 'Inspiring Women' dolls honoring Rosa Parks, Sally Ride |last=Caviness |first=Sarah |date=August 27, 2019 |publisher=[[WJLA 24/7 News]] |access-date=August 27, 2019 |archive-date=August 27, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827124216/https://wjla.com/news/entertainment/barbie-launches-new-inspiring-women-dolls-honoring-rosa-parks-sally-ride |url-status=live }}</ref>
* On October 21, 2019, the play ''Dr. Ride's American Beach House'' by playwright Liza Birkenmeier premiered [[off-Broadway]] at [[Barrow Street Theatre|Ars Nova's Greenwich House Theater]] in New York City. The play is set the evening before Ride's 1983 space flight, and is about women's desires and American norms of sex and power, lensed with Ride's experience as an astronaut in relation to her sex and identity. The title of the play alludes to NASA's [[astronaut beach house]] where astronauts were quarantined before missions.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Liza Birkenmeier's Doctor Ride's American Beach House Begins Off-Broadway |first=Olivia |last=Clement |magazine=[[Playbill]] |issn=0551-0678 |date=October 21, 2019 |url=https://playbill.com/article/liza-birkenmeiers-doctor-rides-american-beach-house-begins-off-broadway |access-date=May 11, 2023 |archive-date=May 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230511124039/https://playbill.com/article/liza-birkenmeiers-doctor-rides-american-beach-house-begins-off-broadway |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=The Final Frontier of Liza Birkenmeier |first=Trish |last=Harnetiaux |magazine=[[The Brooklyn Rail]] |issn=2157-2151 |date=November 2019 |url=https://brooklynrail.org/2019/11/theater/The-Final-Frontier-of-Liza-Birkenmeier |access-date=May 11, 2023 }}</ref>
* In the film ''[[Valley Girl (2020 film)|Valley Girl]]'' (2020), Ride is referred to not only as the first woman astronaut, but also as a [[valley girl]], since she was from Encino.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Rooney |first1=Dave |title='Valley Girl': Film Review |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/valley-girl-1293430/ |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |issn=0018-3660 |access-date=May 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506084138/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/valley-girl-1293430/ |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |date=May 8, 2020 |quote=...that incorporates a nod to Encino's own Sally Ride... |url-status=live }}</ref>
* In 2021, Ride was featured in the second season of the Apple TV+ streaming series ''[[For All Mankind (TV series)|For All Mankind]]'', where she was played by Ellen Wroe.<ref name="forallmankind">{{cite web |last1=Howell |first1=Elizabeth |title='For All Mankind' sneak peek: Potential space shuttle battle looms in season 2 finale |url=https://www.space.com/for-all-mankind-season-2-finale-episode-preview |website=[[Space.com]] |location=New York City |access-date=May 6, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506084520/https://www.space.com/for-all-mankind-season-2-finale-episode-preview |archive-date=May 6, 2021 |date=April 23, 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the show the first American women to fly in [[outer space|space]] is astronaut Molly Cobb, based on [[Mercury 13]] member [[Jerrie Cobb]], as part of an alternate [[Apollo 15]] mission. Ride serves on the [[maiden flight]] of the space shuttle ''Pathfinder'', a [[Nuclear power in space|nuclear-powered]] spacecraft capable of reaching [[lunar orbit]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 15, 2021 |title='For All Mankind' Exclusive Clip: Ed Baldwin (and Sally Ride) Soar to Space in Pathfinder {{!}} Decider |url=https://decider.com/2021/04/15/for-all-mankind-season-2-episode-9-pathfinder-clip/ |access-date=April 4, 2026 |language=en-US }}</ref>
* On January 28, 2025, [[National Geographic]] premiered a documentary called ''[[Sally (2025 film)|Sally]]'', telling the story of Ride's professional and personal life, primarily through her hidden relationship with Tam O'Shaughnessy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kennedy |first=Lisa |date=February 3, 2025 |title='Sally' Review: Astronaut Sally Ride's Life Partner Shares the Personal Saga of the Public Icon |url=https://variety.com/2025/film/reviews/sally-review-sally-ride-1236294916/ |access-date=February 27, 2025 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-date=February 11, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250211043314/https://variety.com/2025/film/reviews/sally-review-sally-ride-1236294916/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Director Cristina Costantini later said, following president [[Donald Trump]]'s cancelation of all diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) programs intended to help overcome prejudice against people who were LGBTQ, female, and also of darker skin color, that "We made this movie not thinking it was particularly controversial; we had no idea it would be this relevant." Costantini also said, referring to Ride's marriage, "People didn't like women in space, and they especially didn't like single women in space".<ref>{{cite news |last=Simonpillai |first=Radheyan |title='People didn't like women in space': how Sally Ride made history and paid the price |newspaper=The Guardian |date=June 15, 2025 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/jun/15/sally-ride-documentary }}</ref>
